claim: Ventral stress fibers are contractile actomyosin bundles that guide adhesion and morphogenesis of many non-muscle cells.
source: Adhesion and morphogenesis of many non-muscle cells are guided by contractile actomyosin bundles called ventral stress fibers.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a foundational statement about ventral stress fibers.

claim: Stress fibers are mechanosensitive structures.
source: While it is well established that stress fibers are mechanosensitive structures, physical mechanisms by which they assemble, align, and mature have remained elusive.
evidence: The manuscript states this is 'well established' indicating it is established scientific knowledge.

claim: Arcs serve as precursors for ventral stress fibers.
source: Here we show that arcs, which serve as precursors for ventral stress fibers, undergo lateral fusion during their centripetal flow to form thick actomyosin bundles that apply tension to focal adhesions at their ends.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract.

claim: Arcs undergo lateral fusion during their centripetal flow to form thick actomyosin bundles.
source: Here we show that arcs, which serve as precursors for ventral stress fibers, undergo lateral fusion during their centripetal flow to form thick actomyosin bundles that apply tension to focal adhesions at their ends.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by live-cell imaging data.

claim: Thick actomyosin bundles formed from arc fusion apply tension to focal adhesions at their ends.
source: Here we show that arcs, which serve as precursors for ventral stress fibers, undergo lateral fusion during their centripetal flow to form thick actomyosin bundles that apply tension to focal adhesions at their ends.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by traction force microscopy data.

claim: Myosin II-derived force inhibits vectorial actin polymerization at focal adhesions through AMPK-mediated phosphorylation of VASP.
source: Importantly, this myosin II-derived force inhibits vectorial actin polymerization at focal adhesions through AMPK-mediated phosphorylation of VASP, and thereby halts stress fiber elongation and ensures their proper contractility.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by multiple experimental approaches including FRAP, photoactivation, and Western blotting.

claim: Inhibition of vectorial actin polymerization halts stress fiber elongation.
source: Importantly, this myosin II-derived force inhibits vectorial actin polymerization at focal adhesions through AMPK-mediated phosphorylation of VASP, and thereby halts stress fiber elongation and ensures their proper contractility.
evidence: This is stated as a consequence of VASP phosphorylation in the abstract.

claim: Inhibition of vectorial actin polymerization ensures proper contractility of stress fibers.
source: Importantly, this myosin II-derived force inhibits vectorial actin polymerization at focal adhesions through AMPK-mediated phosphorylation of VASP, and thereby halts stress fiber elongation and ensures their proper contractility.
evidence: This is stated as a consequence of VASP phosphorylation in the abstract.

claim: Stress fiber maturation requires ADF/cofilin-mediated disassembly of non-contractile stress fibers.
source: Stress fiber maturation additionally requires ADF/cofilin-mediated disassembly of non-contractile stress fibers, whereas contractile fibers are protected from severing.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by cofilin localization and knockdown experiments.

claim: Contractile stress fibers are protected from ADF/cofilin-mediated severing.
source: Stress fiber maturation additionally requires ADF/cofilin-mediated disassembly of non-contractile stress fibers, whereas contractile fibers are protected from severing.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by cofilin localization data showing its absence from contractile fibers.

claim: Myosin-derived tension controls both actin filament assembly and disassembly to ensure generation and proper alignment of contractile stress fibers in migrating cells.
source: Taken together, these data reveal that myosin-derived tension precisely controls both actin filament assembly and disassembly to ensure generation and proper alignment of contractile stress fibers in migrating cells.
evidence: This is the main conclusion stated in the abstract, synthesizing the findings.

claim: Cell migration is essential for embryonic development, wound healing, immunological processes and cancer metastasis.
source: Cell migration is essential for embryonic development, wound healing, immunological processes and cancer metastasis.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: Cell migration is driven by assembly and disassembly of protrusive and contractile actin filament structures.
source: Cell migration is driven by assembly and disassembly of protrusive and contractile actin filament structures.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: Force in protrusive actin filament structures is generated through actin polymerization against the plasma membrane.
source: The force in protrusive actin filament structures, including lamellipodium and filopodia at the leading edge of cell, is generated through actin polymerization against the plasma membrane.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: Force in contractile actin filament bundles is generated by sliding of bipolar myosin II bundles along actin filaments.
source: In contractile actin filament bundles, such as stress fibers, the force is generated by sliding of bipolar myosin II bundles along actin filaments.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: Assembly mechanisms of protrusive actin filament structures are relatively well understood.
source: Notably, whereas the assembly-mechanisms of protrusive actin filament structures are relatively well understood, general principles underlying the assembly of contractile actomyosin bundles have remained elusive (Pollard and Cooper, 2009; Bugyi and Carlier, 2010; Michelot and Drubin, 2011; Burridge and Wittchen, 2013).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations indicating it is established knowledge in the field.

claim: General principles underlying the assembly of contractile actomyosin bundles have remained elusive.
source: Notably, whereas the assembly-mechanisms of protrusive actin filament structures are relatively well understood, general principles underlying the assembly of contractile actomyosin bundles have remained elusive (Pollard and Cooper, 2009; Bugyi and Carlier, 2010; Michelot and Drubin, 2011; Burridge and Wittchen, 2013).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations indicating a gap in knowledge that the study addresses.

claim: Stress fibers are the most prominent contractile actomyosin structures in most cultured non-muscle cells.
source: The most prominent contractile actomyosin structures in most cultured non-muscle cells are stress fibers.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: Stress fibers guide adhesion, mechanotransduction, endothelial barrier integrity, myofibril assembly, and receptor clustering in T-lymphocytes.
source: Beyond cell migration, stress fibers guide adhesion, mechanotransduction, endothelial barrier integrity, myofibril assembly, and receptor clustering in T-lymphocytes (Burridge and Wittchen, 2013; Wong et al., 1983; Sanger et al., 2005; Tojkander et al., 2012; Yi et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations indicating established knowledge.

claim: Stress fibers can be divided into three main categories based on their protein compositions and interactions with focal adhesions.
source: Stress fibers can be divided into three main categories based on their protein compositions and interactions with focal adhesions (Small et al., 1998).
evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation indicating established knowledge.

claim: Dorsal stress fibers are connected to focal adhesions at their distal ends and rise towards the dorsal surface of the cell at their proximal region.
source: Dorsal (radial) stress fibers are connected to focal adhesions at their distal ends and rise towards the dorsal surface of the cell at their proximal region (Hotulainen and Lappalainen, 2006).
evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation indicating established knowledge.

claim: Dorsal stress fibers elongate through vectorial actin polymerization at focal adhesions.
source: They elongate through vectorial actin polymerization at focal adhesions (i.e. coordinated polymerization of actin filaments, whose rapidly elongating barbed ends are facing the focal adhesion, is responsible for growth of dorsal stress fibers).
evidence: This is stated with a clarifying explanation in the introduction.

claim: Dorsal stress fibers do not contain myosin II.
source: These actin filament bundles do not contain myosin II, and dorsal stress fibers are thus unable to contract (Hotulainen and Lappalainen, 2006; Cramer et al., 1997; Tojkander et al., 2011; Oakes et al., 2012; Tee et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations indicating established knowledge.

claim: Dorsal stress fibers are unable to contract.
source: These actin filament bundles do not contain myosin II, and dorsal stress fibers are thus unable to contract (Hotulainen and Lappalainen, 2006; Cramer et al., 1997; Tojkander et al., 2011; Oakes et al., 2012; Tee et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations indicating established knowledge.

claim: Dorsal stress fibers interact with contractile transverse arcs and link them to focal adhesions.
source: However, dorsal stress fibers interact with contractile transverse arcs and link them to focal adhesions.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: Transverse arcs are curved actin bundles which display periodic α-actinin – myosin II pattern.
source: Transverse arcs are curved actin bundles, which display periodic α-actinin – myosin II pattern and undergo retrograde flow towards the cell center in migrating cells.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: Transverse arcs undergo retrograde flow towards the cell center in migrating cells.
source: Transverse arcs are curved actin bundles, which display periodic α-actinin – myosin II pattern and undergo retrograde flow towards the cell center in migrating cells.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: Transverse arcs are derived from α-actinin- and tropomyosin/myosin II- decorated actin filament populations nucleated at the lamellipodium of motile cells.
source: They are derived from α-actinin- and tropomyosin/myosin II- decorated actin filament populations nucleated at the lamellipodium of motile cells (Hotulainen and Lappalainen, 2006; Tojkander et al., 2011; Burnette et al., 2011; 2014).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations indicating established knowledge.

claim: In fibroblasts and melanoma cells, filopodial actin bundles can be recycled for formation of transverse arc-like contractile actomyosin bundles.
source: In fibroblasts and melanoma cells, filopodial actin bundles can be recycled for formation of transverse arc –like contractile actomyosin bundles (Nemethova et al., 2008; Anderson et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations indicating established knowledge.

claim: Ventral stress fibers are contractile actomyosin bundles anchored to focal adhesions at both ends.
source: Ventral stress fibers are defined as contractile actomyosin bundles, which are anchored to focal adhesions at their both ends.
evidence: This is stated as a definition in the introduction.

claim: The central regions of ventral stress fibers can bend towards the dorsal surface of the lamellum.
source: Despite their nomenclature, the central regions of ventral stress fibers can bend towards the dorsal surface of the lamellum (Hotulainen and Lappalainen, 2006; Schulze et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations indicating established knowledge.

claim: Migrating cells display thick ventral stress fibers that are typically oriented perpendicularly to the direction of migration.
source: Migrating cells display thick ventral stress fibers that are typically oriented perpendicularly to the direction of migration, and thinner ventral stress fibers that are often located at the cell rear or below the nucleus.
evidence: This is stated as an observation in the introduction.

claim: Thick ventral stress fibers constitute the major force-generating actomyosin bundles in migrating cells.
source: At least the thick ventral stress fibers, which constitute the major force-generating actomyosin bundles in migrating cells, are derived from the pre-existing network of dorsal stress fibers and transverse arcs.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: Thick ventral stress fibers are derived from the pre-existing network of dorsal stress fibers and transverse arcs.
source: At least the thick ventral stress fibers, which constitute the major force-generating actomyosin bundles in migrating cells, are derived from the pre-existing network of dorsal stress fibers and transverse arcs. However, the underlying mechanism has remained poorly understood (Burridge et al., 2013; Hotulainen and Lappalainen, 2006).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations indicating established knowledge, though the mechanism was not understood.

claim: Stress fibers are typically present only in cells grown on rigid substrata.
source: Stress fibers are typically present only in cells grown on rigid substrata and they disassemble upon cell detachment from the matrix (Mochitate et al., 1991; Discher et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations indicating established knowledge.

claim: Stress fibers disassemble upon cell detachment from the matrix.
source: Stress fibers are typically present only in cells grown on rigid substrata and they disassemble upon cell detachment from the matrix (Mochitate et al., 1991; Discher et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations indicating established knowledge.

claim: After applying fluid shear stress, stress fibers align along the orientation of flow direction in endothelial cells.
source: Furthermore, after applying fluid shear stress, stress fibers align along the orientation of flow direction in endothelial cells (Sato and Ohashi, 2005).
evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation indicating established knowledge.

claim: Focal adhesions develop only on rigid surfaces.
source: Also focal adhesions develop only on rigid surfaces, and applying external tensile force promotes their enlargement (Chrzanowska-Wodnicka and Burridge, 1996; Pelham et al., 1999; Riveline et al., 2001).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations indicating established knowledge.

claim: Applying external tensile force promotes enlargement of focal adhesions.
source: Also focal adhesions develop only on rigid surfaces, and applying external tensile force promotes their enlargement (Chrzanowska-Wodnicka and Burridge, 1996; Pelham et al., 1999; Riveline et al., 2001).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations indicating established knowledge.

claim: Focal adhesions contain several mechano-sensitive proteins, including talin, filamin and p130Cas.
source: Focal adhesions contain several mechano-sensitive proteins, including talin, filamin and p130Cas, whose activities and interactions with other focal adhesion components can be modulated by forces of ~∼10–50 pN range (Sawada et al., 2006; del Rio et al., 2009; Ehrlicher et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations indicating established knowledge.

claim: Activities and interactions of mechano-sensitive focal adhesion proteins can be modulated by forces of ~10–50 pN range.
source: Focal adhesions contain several mechano-sensitive proteins, including talin, filamin and p130Cas, whose activities and interactions with other focal adhesion components can be modulated by forces of ~∼10–50 pN range (Sawada et al., 2006; del Rio et al., 2009; Ehrlicher et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations indicating established knowledge.

claim: Protein compositions of focal adhesions are regulated by tension supplied by myosin II activity and external forces applied to the cell.
source: Furthermore, the protein compositions of focal adhesions are regulated by tension supplied by myosin II activity and external forces applied to the cell (Zaidel-Bar et al., 2007; Kuo et al., 2011; Schiller et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations indicating established knowledge.

claim: Possible effects of tensile forces on actin filament assembly at focal adhesions have remained elusive.
source: Importantly, despite wealth of information concerning mechanosensitive focal adhesion proteins, possible effects of tensile forces on actin filament assembly at focal adhesions have remained elusive.
evidence: This is stated as a gap in knowledge that the study addresses.

claim: Mechanisms by which tension contributes to the alignment of stress fibers have not been reported.
source: Furthermore, the mechanisms by which tension contributes to the alignment of stress fibers and actin dynamics within these actomyosin bundles have not been reported.
evidence: This is stated as a gap in knowledge that the study addresses.

claim: Formation of mature contractile actin bundles from their precursors is a mechanosensitive process.
source: Here we reveal that formation of mature contractile actin bundles from their precursors is a mechanosensitive process.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the introduction.

claim: Arc fusion during centripetal flow is accompanied by increased contractility.
source: We show that arc fusion during centripetal flow is accompanied by increased contractility that inhibits vectorial actin polymerization at focal adhesions through AMPK-mediated phosphorylation of VASP, thus insuring formation of ventral stress fibers.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the introduction and supported by traction force microscopy data.

claim: Activation of AMPK allows generation of contractile ventral stress fibers in cells growing on compliant matrix.
source: Conversely, activation of AMPK allows generation of contractile ventral stress fibers in cells growing on compliant matrix, where their formation is normally prevented.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the introduction and supported by AICAR treatment experiments.

claim: Dorsal stress fibers and arcs are present in U2OS cells grown on compliant matrix.
source: By plating U2OS cells on soft (0.5 kPa) and stiff (64 kPa) substrata, we revealed that dorsal stress fibers and arcs are also present in cells grown on compliant matrix.
evidence: This is a finding from experiments comparing cells on different substrate stiffnesses.

claim: Ventral stress fiber assembly is compromised in U2OS cells grown on compliant matrix.
source: In contrast, ventral stress fiber assembly is compromised under these conditions (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a finding from experiments comparing cells on different substrate stiffnesses, with supporting figure.

claim: 89% of U2OS cells plated on 64 kPa matrix contained ventral stress fibers.
source: While 89% of cells plated on 64 kPa matrix contained ventral stress fibers, only 10% of cells plated on 0.5 kPa matrix exhibited ventral stress fibers as defined by presence of straight, contractile actin bundles connected to focal adhesions at each end.
evidence: This is quantitative data from experiments on different substrate stiffnesses.

claim: Only 10% of U2OS cells plated on 0.5 kPa matrix exhibited ventral stress fibers.
source: While 89% of cells plated on 64 kPa matrix contained ventral stress fibers, only 10% of cells plated on 0.5 kPa matrix exhibited ventral stress fibers as defined by presence of straight, contractile actin bundles connected to focal adhesions at each end.
evidence: This is quantitative data from experiments on different substrate stiffnesses.

claim: Generation of ventral stress fibers is the mechanosensitive phase in the formation of the stress fiber network.
source: Thus, generation of ventral stress fibers appears to be the mechanosensitive phase in the formation of the stress fiber network.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the substrate stiffness experiments.

claim: Thin arc precursors fuse with each other during centripetal flow.
source: Interestingly, live-imaging of GFP-CaP3 -transfected cells revealed that the thin arc precursors fused with each other to form thicker actomyosin bundles during their flow towards the cell center (Figure 1B; Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a finding from live-cell imaging experiments.

claim: Arc fusion often initiates at the sites where arcs are connected to elongating dorsal stress fibers.
source: Fusion appeared to often initiate at the sites where arcs were connected to elongating dorsal stress fibers (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is an observation from live-cell imaging experiments.

claim: Homotypic coalescence of tropomyosin-4/myosin II foci and α-actinin foci of adjacent arcs occurs during the fusion process.
source: Live-imaging of cells expressing CFP-α-actinin and YFP-tropomyosin-4 demonstrated that homotypic coalescence of tropomyosin-4/myosin II foci and α-actinin foci of adjacent arcs occurred during the fusion process in all observed cases (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is a finding from live-cell imaging experiments with dual-labeled cells.

claim: The periodic α-actinin — myosin II pattern is retained during arc fusion.
source: Thus, thin arc precursors fuse with each other during centripetal flow to generate thicker actomyosin bundles, where the periodic α-actinin — myosin II pattern is retained.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the live-cell imaging experiments showing homotypic coalescence.

claim: Thick ventral stress fibers exhibit stronger traction forces to focal adhesions compared to forces applied by dorsal stress fibers.
source: These experiments revealed that thick ventral stress fibers exhibit stronger traction forces to focal adhesions as compared to forces applied by dorsal stress fibers (Figure 2A and B), similarly to what was recently demonstrated with model-based traction force microscopy by Soine et al. (2015).
evidence: This is a finding from traction force microscopy experiments.

claim: Spacing between individual CaP-3 foci decreases as arcs flow towards the cell center and become thicker.
source: Furthermore, spacing between individual CaP-3 foci, which co-localize with α-actinin in stress fibers (Small and Gimona, 1998), decreased as the arcs flowed towards the cell center and become thicker as detected both from several fixed samples and live-cell imaging experiments (representative examples are shown Figure 1—figure supplement 1C and D).
evidence: This is a finding from both fixed and live-cell imaging experiments.

claim: Decreased spacing between CaP-3 foci correlates with increased contractility of arcs.
source: This correlates well with the increased contractility of the structures (Aratyn-Schaus et al., 2011).
evidence: This is an inference supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Distal focal adhesions linked via dorsal stress fibers to the ends of arcs turn and align along the direction of the arc during maturation.
source: These experiments revealed that the 'distal' focal adhesions, linked via dorsal stress fibers to the ends of the arc, turned and aligned along the direction of arc.
evidence: This is a finding from live-cell imaging experiments tracking focal adhesion alignment.

claim: Focal adhesions linked to the central region of arcs do not display alignment during arc maturation.
source: In contrast, focal adhesions linked to the central region of the arc did not display similar alignment during the process.
evidence: This is a finding from live-cell imaging experiments tracking focal adhesion alignment.

claim: Alignment of distal focal adhesions correlates with arc fusion.
source: Alignment of 'distal' focal adhesions correlated with arc fusion, and was accompanied by enlargement of adhesions (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This is a finding from live-cell imaging experiments.

claim: Alignment of distal focal adhesions is accompanied by enlargement of adhesions.
source: Alignment of 'distal' focal adhesions correlated with arc fusion, and was accompanied by enlargement of adhesions (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This is a finding from live-cell imaging experiments.

claim: Arc fusion during centripetal flow correlates with increased contractility, consequent enlargement of distal focal adhesions and their alignment along the direction of the actomyosin bundle.
source: Thus, arc fusion during centripetal flow correlates with their increased contractility, consequent enlargement of distal focal adhesions and their alignment along the direction of the actomyosin bundle.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the traction force and focal adhesion alignment experiments.

claim: Arc fusion leads to formation of a directed ventral stress fiber containing one properly aligned large focal adhesion at both ends.
source: Eventually, this leads to formation of a directed ventral stress fiber, containing one properly aligned large focal adhesion at its both ends.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the live-cell imaging experiments tracking the maturation process.

claim: Dorsal stress fibers in U2OS cells elongate through vectorial actin polymerization at focal adhesions with a rate of ∼0.25 μm/min.
source: In U2OS cells, this 'vectorial' actin polymerization promotes elongation of the actin filament bundle with a rate of ∼0.25 μm/min (Hotulainen and Lappalainen, 2006).
evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation indicating established knowledge from previous work.

claim: Focal adhesions may contain actin filament populations not directly associated with vectorial actin polymerization and elongation of dorsal stress fibers.
source: In addition, focal adhesions may contain other actin filament populations that are not directly associated with vectorial actin polymerization and consequent elongation of dorsal stress fibers.
evidence: This is stated as a consideration based on the presence of multiple tropomyosin isoforms and actin-regulating proteins in focal adhesions.

claim: Several tropomyosin isoforms localize to focal adhesions.
source: This is because several tropomyosin isoforms, which are likely to decorate distinct actin filament populations, localize to focal adhesions (Tojkander et al., 2011) and because several proteins involved in actin polymerization regulate actin dynamics at focal adhesions (e.g. Hotulainen and Lappalainen, 2006; Skau et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations indicating established knowledge.

claim: FRAP experiments performed at focal adhesions show rapid, uniform recovery of GFP-actin fluorescence.
source: Furthermore, FRAP experiments performed at focal adhesions show rapid, uniform recovery of GFP-actin fluorescence (Videos 1 and 2; Figure 2—figure supplement 2), whereas FRAP experiments performed at dorsal stress fiber regions below focal adhesions exhibit treadmilling-like recovery that is indicative of vectorial actin polymerization (Hotulainen and Lappalainen, 2006; Tee et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a finding from FRAP experiments.

claim: FRAP experiments performed at dorsal stress fiber regions below focal adhesions exhibit treadmilling-like recovery indicative of vectorial actin polymerization.
source: Furthermore, FRAP experiments performed at focal adhesions show rapid, uniform recovery of GFP-actin fluorescence (Videos 1 and 2; Figure 2—figure supplement 2), whereas FRAP experiments performed at dorsal stress fiber regions below focal adhesions exhibit treadmilling-like recovery that is indicative of vectorial actin polymerization (Hotulainen and Lappalainen, 2006; Tee et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a finding from FRAP experiments with supporting citations.

claim: Ventral stress fibers do not elongate through vectorial actin polymerization at focal adhesions.
source: Therefore, in contrast to dorsal stress fibers, ventral stress fibers do not elongate through vectorial actin polymerization at focal adhesions.
evidence: This is a conclusion from FRAP and photoactivation experiments comparing dorsal and ventral stress fibers.

claim: MLCK inhibitor ML-7 induces rapid disassembly of most contractile ventral stress fibers and transverse arcs without affecting integrity of non-contractile dorsal stress fibers.
source: This compound induced rapid disassembly of most contractile ventral stress fibers and transverse arcs, without affecting integrity of non-contractile dorsal stress fibers (Figure 2—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: This is a finding from inhibitor treatment experiments.

claim: Dorsal stress fibers in cells treated for 2 h with ML-7 are ∼1.5 times longer compared to control cells.
source: Importantly, dorsal stress fibers in cells treated for 2 h with ML-7 were ∼1.5 times longer compared to the ones in control cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This is quantitative data from inhibitor treatment experiments.

claim: Disruption of contractile stress fibers by ROCK inhibitor Y27632 leads to formation of abnormally long dorsal stress fibers.
source: Similarly, disruption of contractile stress fibers by ROCK inhibitor, Y27632, or by over-expression of dominant inactive Rif GTPase (Rif-TN), which prevents assembly of contractile arcs (Tojkander et al., 2011), led to formation of abnormally long dorsal stress fibers (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A and B, and Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is a finding from inhibitor treatment experiments.

claim: Over-expression of dominant inactive Rif GTPase (Rif-TN) prevents assembly of contractile arcs.
source: Similarly, disruption of contractile stress fibers by ROCK inhibitor, Y27632, or by over-expression of dominant inactive Rif GTPase (Rif-TN), which prevents assembly of contractile arcs (Tojkander et al., 2011), led to formation of abnormally long dorsal stress fibers (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A and B, and Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation indicating established knowledge.

claim: Over-expression of dominant inactive Rif GTPase (Rif-TN) leads to formation of abnormally long dorsal stress fibers.
source: Similarly, disruption of contractile stress fibers by ROCK inhibitor, Y27632, or by over-expression of dominant inactive Rif GTPase (Rif-TN), which prevents assembly of contractile arcs (Tojkander et al., 2011), led to formation of abnormally long dorsal stress fibers (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A and B, and Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is a finding from overexpression experiments.

claim: Abnormally long dorsal stress fibers in Rif-TN expressing cells continue to elongate throughout the entire observation period.
source: Importantly, live-imaging of GFP-actin expressing cells revealed that the abnormally long dorsal stress in Rif-TN transfected cells continued to elongate throughout the entire observation period.
evidence: This is a finding from live-cell imaging experiments.

claim: Dorsal stress fibers in Rif-TN expressing cells occasionally bend or fuse with another elongating dorsal stress fiber during their uncontrolled elongation.
source: During their uncontrolled elongation, the dorsal stress fibers of Rif-TN expressing cells occasionally bent or fused with another elongating dorsal stress fiber initiated from the opposite side of the cell (Figure 2—figure supplement 4A; Videos 3 and 4).
evidence: This is an observation from live-cell imaging experiments.

claim: Ablated ventral stress fibers display approximately 10-fold higher rate of vectorial actin polymerization compared to intact contractile fibers.
source: Whereas vectorial actin polymerization in intact contractile fibers was very slow (∼0,02 μm/min), ablated ventral stress fibers displayed approximately 10-fold higher rate of vectorial actin polymerization (∼0,23 μm/min), which is comparable to the one of dorsal stress fibers (Figure 3A and B, and data not shown).
evidence: This is quantitative data from laser ablation and FRAP experiments.

claim: Vectorial actin polymerization in intact contractile ventral stress fibers is very slow (∼0.02 μm/min).
source: Whereas vectorial actin polymerization in intact contractile fibers was very slow (∼0,02 μm/min), ablated ventral stress fibers displayed approximately 10-fold higher rate of vectorial actin polymerization (∼0,23 μm/min), which is comparable to the one of dorsal stress fibers (Figure 3A and B, and data not shown).
evidence: This is quantitative data from FRAP experiments.

claim: Ablated ventral stress fibers display vectorial actin polymerization at a rate of ∼0.23 μm/min.
source: Whereas vectorial actin polymerization in intact contractile fibers was very slow (∼0,02 μm/min), ablated ventral stress fibers displayed approximately 10-fold higher rate of vectorial actin polymerization (∼0,23 μm/min), which is comparable to the one of dorsal stress fibers (Figure 3A and B, and data not shown).
evidence: This is quantitative data from laser ablation and FRAP experiments.

claim: Photoactivation experiments demonstrate specific elongation of laser ablated ventral stress fibers.
source: Importantly, also photoactivation experiments on PA-GFP-actin expressing cells demonstrated specific elongation of laser ablated ventral stress fibers and lack of vectorial actin polymerization at the focal adhesions located at the ends of non-ablated ventral stress fibers within the same cell (Figure 3C and D).
evidence: This is a finding from photoactivation experiments.

claim: Non-ablated ventral stress fibers lack vectorial actin polymerization at focal adhesions.
source: Importantly, also photoactivation experiments on PA-GFP-actin expressing cells demonstrated specific elongation of laser ablated ventral stress fibers and lack of vectorial actin polymerization at the focal adhesions located at the ends of non-ablated ventral stress fibers within the same cell (Figure 3C and D).
evidence: This is a finding from photoactivation experiments.

claim: Vectorial actin filament assembly that promotes elongation of dorsal stress fibers is inhibited in focal adhesions located at the tips of contractile ventral stress fibers.
source: These data demonstrate that vectorial actin filament assembly, which promotes elongation of dorsal stress fibers, is inhibited in focal adhesions located at the tips of contractile ventral stress fibers.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the FRAP and photoactivation experiments.

claim: Tension applied by myosin II–mediated contractility is important for inhibition of vectorial actin polymerization at focal adhesions located at the ends of ventral stress fibers.
source: Furthermore, laser ablation experiments as well as assays with MLCK and ROCK inhibitors, and dominant inactive Rif provide evidence that tension applied by myosin II–mediated contractility is important for inhibition of vectorial actin polymerization at focal adhesions located at the ends of ventral stress fibers.
evidence: This is a conclusion from multiple experimental approaches.

claim: Dia1 formin has been linked to actin polymerization in focal adhesions.
source: Two proteins promoting actin filament elongation, Dia1 formin and vasodilator-stimulated phosphoprotein (VASP), have been linked to actin polymerization in focal adhesions (Hotulainen and Lappalainen, 2006; Oakes et al., 2012; Watanabe et al., 1999; Gateva et al., 2014; Figure 4—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations indicating established knowledge.

claim: VASP has been linked to actin polymerization in focal adhesions.
source: Two proteins promoting actin filament elongation, Dia1 formin and vasodilator-stimulated phosphoprotein (VASP), have been linked to actin polymerization in focal adhesions (Hotulainen and Lappalainen, 2006; Oakes et al., 2012; Watanabe et al., 1999; Gateva et al., 2014; Figure 4—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations indicating established knowledge.

claim: VASP and its family members Mena and Evl accumulate to focal adhesions.
source: Because from these proteins only VASP, and its family members Mena and Evl, accumulate to focal adhesions (Reinhard et al., 1992; Gertler et al., 1996; Lambrechts et al., 2000; Hoffman et al., 2006), we focused on examining the possible role of VASP in tension-controlled actin filament assembly in focal adhesions.
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations indicating established knowledge.

claim: Zyxin mediates recruitment of VASP to the sites of stress fiber repair and remodelling.
source: Previous studies demonstrated zyxin-mediated recruitment of VASP to the sites of stress fiber repair and remodelling (Smith et al., 2010; Hoffman et al., 2012) and mechanosensitive recruitment of VASP to epithelial zonula adherens (Leerberg et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations indicating established knowledge.

claim: VASP is recruited to epithelial zonula adherens in a mechanosensitive manner.
source: Previous studies demonstrated zyxin-mediated recruitment of VASP to the sites of stress fiber repair and remodelling (Smith et al., 2010; Hoffman et al., 2012) and mechanosensitive recruitment of VASP to epithelial zonula adherens (Leerberg et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation indicating established knowledge.

claim: VASP localizes to focal adhesions located at the tips of both dorsal and ventral stress fibers.
source: Immunofluorescence microscopy revealed that VASP localizes to focal adhesions located at the tips of both dorsal and ventral stress fibers (Figure 4A and B).
evidence: This is a finding from immunofluorescence experiments.

claim: Regulation of VASP localization does not explain the lack of vectorial actin polymerization at the tips of ventral stress fibers.
source: Therefore, regulation of VASP localization does not offer an explanation for the lack of vectorial actin polymerization at the tips of ventral stress fibers.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the VASP localization experiments.

claim: Phosphorylation of VASP at Ser239 and Thr278 inhibits its actin filament binding and polymerization activities.
source: Interestingly, previous work demonstrated that phosphorylation of specific residues (Ser239 and Thr278) of VASP inhibit its actin filament binding and polymerization activities (Harbeck et al., 2000; Benz et al., 2009; Figure 4C).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations indicating established knowledge.

claim: Phospho-Ser239 VASP is enriched in focal adhesions located at the tips of ventral stress fibers.
source: Although the signal with this antibody was weak, it specifically stained focal adhesions located at the tips of ventral stress fibers, whereas enrichment of phospho-Ser239 VASP to adhesions at the tips of dorsal stress fibers was not detected (Figure 4D, E and F).
evidence: This is a finding from immunofluorescence experiments.

claim: Phospho-Ser239 VASP is not enriched in focal adhesions at the tips of dorsal stress fibers.
source: Although the signal with this antibody was weak, it specifically stained focal adhesions located at the tips of ventral stress fibers, whereas enrichment of phospho-Ser239 VASP to adhesions at the tips of dorsal stress fibers was not detected (Figure 4D, E and F).
evidence: This is a finding from immunofluorescence experiments.

claim: Phospho-Ser239 VASP levels are >2-fold elevated in cells transfected with dominant active RhoA.
source: In line with the data presented above, both phospo-Ser239 (Figure 4G and H) and phospho-Thr278 (data not shown) levels were >2-fold elevated in the cell population transfected with a construct expressing dominant active RhoA, whereas phospo-Ser239 levels were ∼5-fold diminished in cells plated on soft matrix and unable to form contractile ventral stress fibers (Figure 4I and J).
evidence: This is quantitative data from Western blotting experiments.

claim: Phospho-Ser239 VASP levels are ∼5-fold diminished in cells plated on soft matrix.
source: In line with the data presented above, both phospo-Ser239 (Figure 4G and H) and phospho-Thr278 (data not shown) levels were >2-fold elevated in the cell population transfected with a construct expressing dominant active RhoA, whereas phospo-Ser239 levels were ∼5-fold diminished in cells plated on soft matrix and unable to form contractile ventral stress fibers (Figure 4I and J).
evidence: This is quantitative data from Western blotting experiments.

claim: VASP phosphorylation in focal adhesions correlates with increased contractility of stress fibers.
source: Thus, VASP phosphorylation in focal adhesions correlates with increased contractility of stress fibers.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the Western blotting and immunofluorescence experiments.

claim: VASP phosphorylation at Ser239 and Thr278 is regulated by cAMP- and cGMP dependent protein kinases PKA and PKG as well as by AMP-activated Protein Kinase (AMPK).
source: VASP phosphorylation at Ser239 and Thr278 is regulated by cAMP- and cGMP dependent protein kinases PKA and PKG as well as by AMP-activated Protein Kinase (AMPK) (Butt et al., 1994; Blume et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations indicating established knowledge.

claim: AMPK inhibitors compound C and KT5823 inhibit VASP phosphorylation at Ser239 and Thr278.
source: Both of compound C and KT5823 inhibited VASP phosphorylation at Ser239 and Thr278 (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is a finding from Western blotting experiments with inhibitors.

claim: Incubation of U2OS cells for 4 hr with compound C or KT5823 results in a nearly complete lack of contractile ventral stress fibers.
source: Importantly, incubation of U2OS cells for 4 hr in the presence of these inhibitors resulted in a nearly complete lack of contractile ventral stress fibers and defects in arc fusion.
evidence: This is a finding from inhibitor treatment experiments.

claim: Incubation of U2OS cells for 4 hr with compound C or KT5823 results in defects in arc fusion.
source: Importantly, incubation of U2OS cells for 4 hr in the presence of these inhibitors resulted in a nearly complete lack of contractile ventral stress fibers and defects in arc fusion.
evidence: This is a finding from inhibitor treatment experiments.

claim: Compound C and KT5823 promote formation of abnormally long dorsal stress fibers.
source: Furthermore, these inhibitors promoted formation of abnormally long dorsal stress fibers, which often bent at their proximal regions (Figure 5A and B).
evidence: This is a finding from inhibitor treatment experiments.

claim: Cells expressing constitutively active Ser239Ala;Thr278Ala VASP mutant display significantly longer dorsal stress fibers compared to wild-type VASP expressing cells.
source: Also Ser239Ala;Thr278Ala mutant VASP expressing cells displayed significantly longer dorsal stress fibers as compared to wild-type VASP expressing cells (Figure 5D and E).
evidence: This is quantitative data from experiments with mutant VASP.

claim: Over-expression of Ser239Ala;Thr278Ala mutant VASP occasionally results in formation of curly actin filament bundles.
source: Furthermore, over-expression of Ser239Ala;Thr278Ala mutant VASP occasionally resulted in formation of 'curly' actin filament bundles (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is an observation from experiments with mutant VASP.

claim: Inhibition of VASP phosphorylation at Ser239 and Thr278 results in a similar phenotype to inhibition of contractile arc assembly through over-expression of Rif-TN.
source: Thus, inhibition of VASP phosphorylation at Ser239 and Thr278 results in a similar phenotype compared to the one resulting from the inhibition of contractile arc assembly through over-expression of Rif-TN (see Figure 2—figure supplement 4), suggesting that VASP phosphorylation has a key role in tension-controlled actin filament assembly at focal adhesions.
evidence: This is a conclusion from comparing phenotypes of different experimental manipulations.

claim: VASP phosphorylation has a key role in tension-controlled actin filament assembly at focal adhesions.
source: Thus, inhibition of VASP phosphorylation at Ser239 and Thr278 results in a similar phenotype compared to the one resulting from the inhibition of contractile arc assembly through over-expression of Rif-TN (see Figure 2—figure supplement 4), suggesting that VASP phosphorylation has a key role in tension-controlled actin filament assembly at focal adhesions.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the inhibitor and mutant VASP experiments.

claim: Activation of AMPK by AICAR leads to increased Ser239 phosphorylation of VASP.
source: Conversely, activation of AMPK by AICAR (Carling et al., 2008) leads to an increased Ser239 phosphorylation of VASP and early maturation of ventral stress fibers (Figure 6A and B).
evidence: This is a finding from AICAR treatment and Western blotting experiments.

claim: Activation of AMPK by AICAR leads to early maturation of ventral stress fibers.
source: Conversely, activation of AMPK by AICAR (Carling et al., 2008) leads to an increased Ser239 phosphorylation of VASP and early maturation of ventral stress fibers (Figure 6A and B).
evidence: This is a finding from AICAR treatment experiments.

claim: Cells exposed for 16 h to AICAR display shorter dorsal stress fibers compared to control cells.
source: Cells exposed for 16 h to AICAR displayed shorter dorsal stress fibers compared to control cells and their ventral stress fibers were typically located close to cell perimeter (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is a finding from AICAR treatment experiments.

claim: Ventral stress fibers in AICAR-treated cells are typically located close to cell perimeter.
source: Cells exposed for 16 h to AICAR displayed shorter dorsal stress fibers compared to control cells and their ventral stress fibers were typically located close to cell perimeter (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is a finding from AICAR treatment experiments.

claim: The phenotype of AICAR-treated cells is similar to that resulting from depletion of VASP.
source: This phenotype was similar to the one resulting from depletion of VASP (Figure 4—figure supplement 1), suggesting that AICAR indeed affects stress fibers mainly through inducing VASP phosphorylation.
evidence: This is a conclusion from comparing phenotypes of AICAR treatment and VASP depletion.

claim: AICAR affects stress fibers mainly through inducing VASP phosphorylation.
source: This phenotype was similar to the one resulting from depletion of VASP (Figure 4—figure supplement 1), suggesting that AICAR indeed affects stress fibers mainly through inducing VASP phosphorylation.
evidence: This is a conclusion from comparing phenotypes of AICAR treatment and VASP depletion.

claim: Activation of AMPK and VASP phosphorylation by AICAR treatment is sufficient to induce formation of ventral stress fibers on soft (0.5 kPa) matrix.
source: Importantly, activation of AMPK and VASP phosphorylation by AICAR treatment was sufficient to induce the formation of ventral stress fibers on soft (0.5 kPa) matrix, where their formation is normally inhibited (Figure 6C and D).
evidence: This is a finding from AICAR treatment experiments on soft matrix.

claim: VASP is important for mechanosensitive actin filament assembly in focal adhesions.
source: These experiments revealed approximately 3-fold decrease in ablation-induced vectorial actin polymerization at the tips of ventral stress fibers in VASP knockdown cells compared to control cells (Figure 7), demonstrating that VASP is indeed important for mechanosensitive actin filament assembly in focal adhesion.
evidence: This is a conclusion from photoablation experiments in VASP knockdown cells.

claim: VASP knockdown cells show approximately 3-fold decrease in ablation-induced vectorial actin polymerization at the tips of ventral stress fibers compared to control cells.
source: These experiments revealed approximately 3-fold decrease in ablation-induced vectorial actin polymerization at the tips of ventral stress fibers in VASP knockdown cells compared to control cells (Figure 7), demonstrating that VASP is indeed important for mechanosensitive actin filament assembly in focal adhesion.
evidence: This is quantitative data from photoablation experiments in VASP knockdown cells.

claim: AMPK-mediated phosphorylation of VASP is essential for tension-sensitive inhibition of vectorial actin filament assembly at focal adhesions.
source: Together, these results provide evidence that AMPK-mediated phosphorylation of VASP is essential for tension-sensitive inhibition of vectorial actin filament assembly at focal adhesions, and consequent formation and stabilization of ventral stress fibers.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the AMPK inhibitor, AICAR, and VASP experiments.

claim: AMPK-mediated phosphorylation of VASP is essential for formation and stabilization of ventral stress fibers.
source: Together, these results provide evidence that AMPK-mediated phosphorylation of VASP is essential for tension-sensitive inhibition of vectorial actin filament assembly at focal adhesions, and consequent formation and stabilization of ventral stress fibers.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the AMPK inhibitor, AICAR, and VASP experiments.

claim: Maturing arcs are typically connected to several dorsal stress fibers and focal adhesions.
source: Maturing arcs are typically connected to several dorsal stress fibers and focal adhesions, but only the ones located at the ends of the arc bundle are used for the formation of a ventral stress fiber (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an observation from live-cell imaging experiments.

claim: Only focal adhesions located at the ends of the arc bundle are used for the formation of a ventral stress fiber.
source: Maturing arcs are typically connected to several dorsal stress fibers and focal adhesions, but only the ones located at the ends of the arc bundle are used for the formation of a ventral stress fiber (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an observation from live-cell imaging experiments.

claim: Focal adhesions connected to the ends of arcs elongate during maturation of arcs into a ventral stress fiber.
source: Focal adhesions connected to the ends of arcs elongated during maturation of arcs into a ventral stress fiber, whereas adhesions associated with the central region of the arc through dorsal stress fibers diminished in size and eventually disappeared (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from live-cell imaging experiments.

claim: Focal adhesions associated with the central region of arcs through dorsal stress fibers diminish in size and eventually disappear during arc maturation.
source: Focal adhesions connected to the ends of arcs elongated during maturation of arcs into a ventral stress fiber, whereas adhesions associated with the central region of the arc through dorsal stress fibers diminished in size and eventually disappeared (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from live-cell imaging experiments.

claim: Dorsal stress fibers oriented perpendicularly to the contractile arc disassemble during stress fiber maturation.
source: These experiments revealed that dorsal stress fibers, oriented perpendicularly to the contractile arc, sense weaker myosin II -generated tension and disassemble during stress fiber maturation process (Figure 8A and C).
evidence: This is a finding from live-cell imaging experiments.

claim: Dorsal stress fiber regions that reach beyond the contractile arc/ventral stress fiber disassemble during the maturation process.
source: Furthermore, those dorsal stress fiber regions, which reach beyond the contractile arc/ventral stress fiber, disassemble during the process (Figure 8B).
evidence: This is a finding from live-cell imaging experiments.

claim: ADF/cofilin proteins are essential regulators of F-actin disassembly in all eukaryotic cells.
source: Actin depolymerizing factor (ADF)/cofilin proteins are essential regulators of F-actin disassembly in all eukaryotic cells (Poukkula et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation indicating established knowledge.

claim: ADF/cofilins preferentially bind and disassemble flexible actin filaments in vitro.
source: Interestingly, ADF/cofilins were recently shown to preferentially bind and disassemble flexible actin filaments in vitro.
evidence: This is stated as recent knowledge from the literature.

claim: ADF/cofilins do not localize to contractile stress fibers in intact cells.
source: ADF/cofilins did not localize to contractile stress fibers in intact cells, but translocated to stress fibers when pre-stretched elastic substratum was relaxed (Hayakawa et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation indicating established knowledge.

claim: ADF/cofilins translocate to stress fibers when pre-stretched elastic substratum is relaxed.
source: ADF/cofilins did not localize to contractile stress fibers in intact cells, but translocated to stress fibers when pre-stretched elastic substratum was relaxed (Hayakawa et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation indicating established knowledge.

claim: ADF/cofilins affect actin filament bending mechanics.
source: Furthermore, ADF/cofilins affect the actin filament bending mechanics (McCullough et al., 2008; Elam et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations indicating established knowledge.

claim: Cofilin-1 is the major ADF/cofilin isoform in non-muscle cells.
source: The major ADF/cofilin isoform, cofilin-1, is highly abundant protein in non-muscle cells where it displays mainly diffuse cytoplasmic localization.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: Cofilin-1 displays mainly diffuse cytoplasmic localization in non-muscle cells.
source: The major ADF/cofilin isoform, cofilin-1, is highly abundant protein in non-muscle cells where it displays mainly diffuse cytoplasmic localization.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: Endogenous cofilin-1 and flag-tagged cofilin-1 localize to dorsal stress fibers in U2OS cells.
source: Interestingly, endogenous cofilin-1 and flag-tagged cofilin-1 also localized to dorsal stress fibers in U2OS cells, whereas contractile ventral stress fibers and thick arcs did not exhibit detectable enrichment of cofilin-1 (Figure 9A and B; Figure 9—figure supplement 1A, B and C).
evidence: This is a finding from immunofluorescence experiments.

claim: Contractile ventral stress fibers and thick arcs do not exhibit detectable enrichment of cofilin-1.
source: Interestingly, endogenous cofilin-1 and flag-tagged cofilin-1 also localized to dorsal stress fibers in U2OS cells, whereas contractile ventral stress fibers and thick arcs did not exhibit detectable enrichment of cofilin-1 (Figure 9A and B; Figure 9—figure supplement 1A, B and C).
evidence: This is a finding from immunofluorescence experiments.

claim: Cofilin-1 localizes to curly actin filament bundles in cells over-expressing Ser239Ala;Thr278Ala mutant VASP.
source: Furthermore, cofilin-1 localized to the 'curly' actin filament bundles that were occasionally present in cells over-expressing Ser239Ala;Thr278Ala mutant VASP (Figure 9—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is a finding from immunofluorescence experiments.

claim: Curly actin filament bundles in cells over-expressing Ser239Ala;Thr278Ala mutant VASP contain myosin II but exert defective contractile properties.
source: These bundles contain myosin II, but exert defective contractile properties as detected by live cell imaging (data not shown).
evidence: This is an observation from live-cell imaging experiments.

claim: Cofilin-1 localizes specifically to dorsal stress fibers and other non-contractile actin bundles in U2OS cells.
source: Thus, cofilin-1 appears to localize specifically to dorsal stress fibers and other non-contractile actin bundles in U2OS cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the cofilin localization experiments.

claim: Depletion of cofilin-1 leads to defects in multiple actin-based structures such as lamellipodia and sites of endocytosis.
source: Depletion of cofilin-1 leads to defects in multiple actin-based structures such as lamellipodia and sites of endocytosis due to diminished filament disassembly as well as to cortical F-actin accumulation due to excessive myosin II activity (e.g. Hotulainen et al., 2005; Sidani et al., 2007; Kiuchi et al., 2007; Wiggan et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations indicating established knowledge.

claim: Depletion of cofilin-1 from U2OS cells results in appearance of abnormally thick and long dorsal stress fibers.
source: Importantly, depletion of cofilin-1 from U2OS cells resulted also in an appearance of abnormally thick and long dorsal stress fibers (Figure 9C and D; Figure 9—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is a finding from cofilin-1 knockdown experiments.

claim: Fusion of arcs during centripetal flow is diminished in cofilin-1 depleted cells.
source: Furthermore, fusion of arcs during their centripetal flow was diminished, leading to problems in the formation of proper ventral stress fibers (Figure 9—figure supplement 1F; Video 5).
evidence: This is a finding from cofilin-1 knockdown experiments.

claim: Defects in arc fusion in cofilin-1 depleted cells lead to problems in the formation of proper ventral stress fibers.
source: Furthermore, fusion of arcs during their centripetal flow was diminished, leading to problems in the formation of proper ventral stress fibers (Figure 9—figure supplement 1F; Video 5).
evidence: This is a finding from cofilin-1 knockdown experiments.

claim: Proper ADF/cofilin-mediated turnover of dorsal stress fibers is required for proper coalescence of dorsal stress fiber–associated arcs.
source: Defects in arcs fusion suggest that proper ADF/cofilin-mediated turnover of dorsal stress fibers is required for proper coalescence of dorsal stress fiber–associated arcs.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the cofilin-1 knockdown experiments.

claim: ADF/cofilins are important for turnover of non-contractile dorsal stress fibers.
source: These data provide evidence that ADF/cofilins are important for turnover of non-contractile dorsal stress fibers, whereas contractile arcs and ventral stress fibers appear to be protected from ADF/cofilin-mediated F-actin disassembly.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the cofilin localization and knockdown experiments.

claim: Contractile arcs and ventral stress fibers appear to be protected from ADF/cofilin-mediated F-actin disassembly.
source: These data provide evidence that ADF/cofilins are important for turnover of non-contractile dorsal stress fibers, whereas contractile arcs and ventral stress fibers appear to be protected from ADF/cofilin-mediated F-actin disassembly.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the cofilin localization experiments showing its absence from contractile structures.

claim: Dorsal stress fibers elongate through vectorial actin polymerization at focal adhesions mediated at least by VASP and Dia1 formin.
source: Dorsal stress fibers are initiated from focal adhesions located at the leading edge of cells, and elongate through 'vectorial' actin polymerization at focal adhesions, mediated at least by VASP and Dia1 formin (Hotulainen and Lappalainen, 2006; Watanabe et al., 1999; Gateva et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations as part of the working model.

claim: VASP at focal adhesions is expected to catalyse polymerization of a unipolar actin filament bundle towards the cell center.
source: Similarly to filopodia, where VASP localizes at the tip-complex and promotes assembly of unipolar actin filament bundles, VASP at focal adhesions is expected to catalyse polymerization of an unipolar actin filament bundle towards the cell center.
evidence: This is an inference based on the known function of VASP in filopodia.

claim: Elongating dorsal stress fibers associate with multiple myosin II containing arcs derived from lamellipodial actin structures.
source: Elongating dorsal stress fibers associate with multiple myosin II containing arcs, which are derived from the lamellipodial actin structures (Figure 10A).
evidence: This is stated as part of the working model based on the study's findings.

claim: Focal adhesions attached via dorsal stress fibers to the ends of contractile arcs sense strong myosin II-generated tension.
source: As a result, those focal adhesions that are attached via dorsal stress fibers to the ends of the contractile arc sense strong myosin II-generated tension, leading to their enlargement and turning along the direction of the arc.
evidence: This is stated as part of the working model based on the study's findings.

claim: Ventral stress fibers apply strong traction forces to the substrate through their terminally located focal adhesions.
source: In support to this, ventral stress fibers apply strong traction forces to the substrate through their terminally located focal adhesions (Figure 2 and Möhl et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated with supporting data and citation.

claim: Tension-mediated maturation of terminal focal adhesions leads to inhibition of vectorial actin polymerization, which is at least partially mediated by phosphorylation of VASP.
source: Moreover, tension-mediated maturation of terminal focal adhesions leads to inhibition of vectorial actin polymerization, which is at least partially mediated by phosphorylation of VASP (Figure 10C).
evidence: This is stated as part of the working model based on the study's findings.

claim: Other proteins besides VASP are likely to contribute to vectorial actin polymerization at focal adhesions.
source: However, because VASP-depletion did not result in a compete inhibition of vectorial actin polymerization after releasing the tension in ventral stress fibers (Figure 7), other proteins are also likely to contribute to vectorial actin polymerization at focal adhesions.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the VASP knockdown experiments.

claim: VASP may contribute to integrity of adhesions at the tips of ventral stress fibers through its actin filament bundling activity.
source: Thus, VASP may contribute to integrity of the adhesions at the tips of ventral stress fibers through its other activities, including actin filament bundling (Bear and Gertler, 2009).
evidence: This is speculation based on known VASP activities.

claim: VASP phosphorylation is not expected to inhibit all actin dynamics in focal adhesions.
source: Furthermore, VASP phosphorylation is not expected to inhibit all actin dynamics in focal adhesions, because VASP appears to specifically contribute to vectorial actin polymerization at focal adhesions, whereas other proteins such as formins may promote the turnover of other focal adhesion-associated actin filament populations.
evidence: This is an inference based on the specific role of VASP and the presence of other actin-regulating proteins.

claim: Inhibition of vectorial actin polymerization is essential for proper alignment and contractility of ventral stress fibers.
source: Importantly, inhibition of vectorial actin polymerization is essential for proper alignment and contractility of the ventral stress fiber, because continuous elongation of the actin filament bundle from focal adhesions would counteract myosin II-driven shortening of the actomyosin bundle.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the study's findings and mechanical reasoning.

claim: Mechanosensitive binding of cofilin-1 to dorsal stress fibers not under myosin II-applied tension leads to disassembly of these non-productive regions.
source: Finally, we propose that mechanosensitive binding of cofilin-1 to those dorsal stress fibers and dorsal stress fiber regions, which are not under myosin II-applied tension, leads to disassembly of these 'non-productive' regions of the stress fiber network.
evidence: This is stated as part of the working model based on the study's findings.

claim: Focal adhesions at the distal ends of central dorsal stress fibers diminish in size and disappear during stress fiber maturation.
source: Consequently, the focal adhesions located at the distal ends of 'central' dorsal stress fibers, which are oriented perpendicularly to the contractile arcs and hence do not sense strong myosin II–derived tension, diminish in size and disappear.
evidence: This is stated as part of the working model based on the study's findings.

claim: Focal adhesions are mechanosensitive structures.
source: Focal adhesions are mechanosensitive structures (e.g. Iskratsch et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation indicating established knowledge.

claim: Maturation of focal adhesions from nascent adhesions and their maintenance require relatively small forces that can be generated by retrograde actin flow without myosin II-driven contractility.
source: Their maturation from nascent adhesions and maintenance require relatively small forces that can be generated by retrograde actin flow without myosin II-driven contractility (Oakes et al., 2012; Stricker et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations indicating established knowledge.

claim: Focal adhesions mature into larger, elongated adhesions under stronger, myosin II-derived tension.
source: However, focal adhesions mature into larger, elongated adhesions under stronger, myosin II-derived tension (Geiger et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation indicating established knowledge.

claim: Myosin II-generated force affects the protein composition and dynamics in focal adhesions.
source: Myosin II -generated force also affects the protein composition and dynamics in focal adhesions (Kuo et al., 2011; Schiller et al., 2011; Wolfenson et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations indicating established knowledge.

claim: Vectorial actin polymerization that drives elongation of stress fibers is strictly controlled in focal adhesions.
source: Here, we provide evidence that vectorial actin polymerization, which drives elongation of stress fibers, is strictly controlled in focal adhesions.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the study's findings.

claim: Different force regimes have distinct effects on actin dynamics and molecular composition of focal adhesions.
source: Thus, different force regimes seem to have distinct effects on actin dynamics and molecular composition of focal adhesions.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the study's findings and discussion of the literature.

claim: Weak forces exerted by retrograde actin flow are required for VASP recruitment and promote vectorial actin polymerization at focal adhesions.
source: While weak forces exerted by retrograde actin flow appear to be required for VASP recruitment and to promote vectorial actin polymerization at focal adhesions, stronger force applied by contractility of the myosin II-containing ventral stress fiber efficiently inhibits actin polymerization at focal adhesions.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the study's findings.

claim: Stronger force applied by contractility of myosin II-containing ventral stress fibers efficiently inhibits actin polymerization at focal adhesions.
source: While weak forces exerted by retrograde actin flow appear to be required for VASP recruitment and to promote vectorial actin polymerization at focal adhesions, stronger force applied by contractility of the myosin II-containing ventral stress fiber efficiently inhibits actin polymerization at focal adhesions.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the study's findings.

claim: VASP is phosphorylated by AMPK during the process of tension-mediated inhibition of actin polymerization at focal adhesions.
source: Importantly, during this process VASP is phosphorylated by AMPK, whose activity at least in muscle cells can be controlled by tension through a currently uncharacterized mechanism (Blair et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated as a finding with a supporting citation about AMPK regulation.

claim: AMPK activity in muscle cells can be controlled by tension through a currently uncharacterized mechanism.
source: Importantly, during this process VASP is phosphorylated by AMPK, whose activity at least in muscle cells can be controlled by tension through a currently uncharacterized mechanism (Blair et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation indicating established knowledge.

claim: Activities or localizations of additional actin-polymerization associated proteins in focal adhesions are likely regulated by contractility.
source: It is likely that activities or localizations of additional actin-polymerization associated proteins in focal adhesions are regulated by contractility.
evidence: This is speculation based on the study's findings.

claim: Palladin, an interaction partner of VASP, is enriched in focal adhesions located at the tips of dorsal stress fibers but absent from adhesions at the tips of ventral stress fibers.
source: Indeed, an interaction partner of VASP, palladin (Gateva et al., 2014), as well as tropomyosins Tm1 and Tm5NM1 (Figure 10—figure supplement 1) are enriched in focal adhesions located at the tips of dorsal stress fibers, but absent from adhesions at the tips of ventral stress fibers.
evidence: This is a finding from immunofluorescence experiments.

claim: Tropomyosins Tm1 and Tm5NM1 are enriched in focal adhesions located at the tips of dorsal stress fibers but absent from adhesions at the tips of ventral stress fibers.
source: Indeed, an interaction partner of VASP, palladin (Gateva et al., 2014), as well as tropomyosins Tm1 and Tm5NM1 (Figure 10—figure supplement 1) are enriched in focal adhesions located at the tips of dorsal stress fibers, but absent from adhesions at the tips of ventral stress fibers.
evidence: This is a finding from immunofluorescence experiments.

claim: Formins contribute to actin filament nucleation and/or processive polymerization in focal adhesions.
source: Furthermore, formins contribute to actin filament nucleation and/or processive polymerization in focal adhesions, and it is likely that also their activities are regulated during this process.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: Low-regime forces (<3 pN) increase the actin polymerization activity of formins.
source: Recent studies demonstrated that low-regime forces (<3 pN) increase the actin polymerization activity of formins (Courtemanche, et al., 2013; Jégou et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations indicating established knowledge.

claim: The activity of formins can be controlled by a local increase in G-actin levels.
source: Furthermore, the activity of formins can be controlled by a local increase in G-actin levels (Higashida et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation indicating established knowledge.

claim: Possible regulation of formin activity in focal adhesions is more likely controlled through biochemical signalling cascades than direct mechanical regulation of the formin molecule.
source: However, similar to shown here for VASP, we propose that possible regulation of formin activity in focal adhesions is more likely controlled through biochemical signalling cascades than direct mechanical regulation of the formin molecule.
evidence: This is speculation based on the study's findings and reasoning.

claim: Culturing cells on hyaluronic acid containing soft gels can produce formation of ventral stress fibers that is otherwise observed only in cells cultured on rigid substrates.
source: This is because culturing cells on hyaluronic acid containing soft gels can produce a similar formation of ventral stress fibers that is otherwise observed only in cells cultured on rigid substrates (Chopra et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation indicating established knowledge.

claim: Several tyrosine kinases play an important role in focal adhesion mechanosensing.
source: Furthermore, several tyrosine kinases play an important role in focal adhesion mechanosensing, and their inactivation can shift the stiffness regime for assembly of large focal adhesions and ventral stress fibers (Prager-Khoutorsky et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation indicating established knowledge.

claim: Inactivation of tyrosine kinases can shift the stiffness regime for assembly of large focal adhesions and ventral stress fibers.
source: Furthermore, several tyrosine kinases play an important role in focal adhesion mechanosensing, and their inactivation can shift the stiffness regime for assembly of large focal adhesions and ventral stress fibers (Prager-Khoutorsky et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation indicating established knowledge.
